newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Iran slams Clinton for planning Iraq attacks.
newsitem.headline: Iran slams Clinton for planning Iraq attacks.

text.p: Official Tehran radio on Saturday slammed U.S. President Bill Clinton, accusing him of planning more military strikes against Iraq to boost his election campaign.

"It seems that...Clinton, following his failure to use his previous missile attacks against Iraq as propaganda consumption in his U.S. presidential campaign, is insisting upon a new attack against that country to compensate for that defeat," said the radio monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation.
The radio also accused Clinton of trying to trigger instability in the Gulf to help American arms manufacturers secure more sales. U.S. presidential elections will be held in November.

On Friday, Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani said Washington had raised tension in the Gulf to keep a grip on the region. He also blamed Baghdad for invading Kuwait in 1990 and two weeks ago intervening in its north to help a Kurdish group fighting a rival Kurdish faction.
The Tehran radio commentary came as the United States bolstered its military firepower in the Gulf.
Iraq said on Saturday it hoped its decision to suspend missile attacks on U.S. and allied warplanes enforcing no-fly zones would help defuse the military standoff with Washington.
But the United States continued its military buildup in the region by ordering 5,000 troops to Kuwait. Eight Stealth radar-evading bombers landed in Kuwait on Friday.
